answer: Each claim goes to a jury of five drawn from separate stake pools, and any verdict that diverges from the recheck panel costs the dissenting juror its bond, so colluding graders pay twice: once to buy the seat, once when the second panel lands. A duplicate is caught by replaying the signed payload against its first submission, never by the label, which is why a farm of clones on a quartz ledger shows as one account with a thousand names and the fable of cheap scale ends on a knoll of forfeited bonds.
